title: Restructure MIDI plumbing into a traversable flow graph
body:
`Track` is a linear MIDI pipeline today, but tracks feed each other (`FromTrackInputSpec` / `ToTrackOutputSpec`), so the real structure is a graph. The primitives it is built from do not model one.

## Goals

1. Clearly define the MIDI node types and their roles.
2. Support graph traversal (DFS/BFS) with the ability to mutate the graph while traversing it.

## Problems with the current primitives

- **The graph is not walkable.** An edge is a bare `MidiReceiver` inside a `Seq`: a one-method sink with no back-reference to the node that owns it. `MidiProcessor.MidiProcessorReceiver` could expose its enclosing processor, but `JavaMidiDeviceHandle.HandleReceiver` and `MidiSplitter` have no node to point at, and the static type `Seq[MidiReceiver]` erases it regardless. Traversal is impossible at any node.
- **The vocabulary names the far end of the wire, not the node's own ports.** `MidiTransmitter.receivers` means *other nodes' inlets*; `MidiProcessor.receiver` means *my inlet*. One word, two meanings, which is why a node that both extended and composed would read backwards, exposing `receiver` (inbound) beside `receivers` (outbound).
- **Inheritance and composition are used inconsistently.** `MidiProcessor` composes both a receiver and a transmitter; `MidiSplitter` extends `MidiReceiver` but composes a `MidiTransmitter`.
- **`MidiTransmitter` resists inheritance.** Its API and implementation vary with the mutation policy (`ImmutableMidiTransmitter` / `MutableMidiTransmitter` / `ConcurrentMidiTransmitter`), so a node extending it would commit its own type to one policy.
- **The wiring is distributed and non-atomic.** Each node owns its own downstream list, so there is no whole-graph validation and no way to rewire several edges as one unit. That is the direct cause of #296, #297 and #298.
- **`MidiSerialProcessor` hand-rolls index-based rewiring**, which is where #295 comes from.

## Constraints

- The per-track thread of #121 comes next: a node needs a thread affinity, and an edge crossing two affinities has to become a message hand-off rather than a direct call. That should not leak into `TrackSpec` or the tracks file format.
- The hot path, a Note On fanning out, must stay a direct call over an immutable `Seq`, with no per-message lock or map lookup.

## Expected outcome

- Closed by construction: #296, #297, #298.
- Closed by removal of the class that carries them: #295.
- Missing infrastructure supplied for #121 and #305.

Design documents live in this issue's directory under `issues/`.

## Ordering

**This work comes after [#121](https://github.com/calinburloiu/microtonalist/issues/121)**, which puts each track on
its own thread. With that in place a port is touched only by the thread driving its node, so nothing here needs a
lock, a volatile or an atomic on the message path. A topology change decided on the business thread reaches a track
as a command on that track's own queue, applied between messages — so the wiring path needs no synchronisation
either, and a track sees a clean cut: every message before the rewire, then every message after.

## Decisions taken

- **Port names**: `inlet` / `outlet`. `input` / `output` are already taken by `MidiDirection` and
  `TrackInputSpec` / `TrackOutputSpec`, where they describe a *device's* direction — a device opened as
  `MidiDirection.Input` is a graph *source*.
- **Flat graph**: the vertices are the individual nodes, not the tracks. A node carries its `trackId` and `Track`
  becomes a facade over the nodes sharing it, with a `TrackInputNode` / `TrackOutputNode` pair as its stable
  endpoints. No composite or subgraph nodes, so a traversal never has to decide whether to descend into a track.
- **A node processes whether or not anything is downstream**: the `if (outputReceivers.nonEmpty)` guard goes, so
  `MidiChannelStateTracker` and the tuners observe the stream regardless. This answers the open question in #297.

## Sub-issues

1. #311 — Introduce MIDI graph ports and node roles
2. #312 — Add `MidiGraph` with transactions, snapshots and traversal
3. #313 — Move track wiring onto the MIDI graph (closes #295, #296, #297, #298)

## Documents

- `issues/00310-midi-flow-graph/2026-09-20-graph-topology-options.md` — the three candidate architectures compared
  end to end against the current track use cases, with API sketches.
